correctness.rationale: For r>=4 the only nonfull resolving neighborhoods are the four-vertex sets from comparing a_i,a_j or b_i,b_j and the x,b_i / y,a_i cross-families; distances confirm kappa=4. Each pair of page sums p_i+p_j>=k; adding all yields total page weight>=rk/2. Uniform internal weight k/4 and zero on spine is feasible. At optimality every pair inequality is tight and g(x)=g(y)=0, forcing p_i=k/2; the only remaining nonautomatic constraints are the two cross inequalities in the claim. For r=4 they collapse to equality forcing alpha_i=beta_i=k/4. For k=4 the page sum=2 forces all internals weight one, and for r>=6, k<=2 two page classes of size at least three give explicit asymmetric optima.

value.rationale: A linear program optimum alone does not describe all equality cases. The explicit necessary-and-sufficient page-weight inequalities classify the geometry of every minimum resolving function at every real k in [1,4], identify a unique four-page exception and exhibit genuinely asymmetric optimizers in large books. These are natural data for robust sensor-placement designs and a complete family classification, not arbitrary finite tabulation.

scientific_limitations: Exactly r>=4 square-page books and real k in [1,4], with box weights [0,1]; scalar value is credited to earlier implications, not claimed wholly new.
A differently named generalized-theta all-minimizer classification could already cover this LP polytope.
